title: You Will Testify
author: Jonny Ardavanis
excerpt: Jesus doesn't say you should testify, or could. He says you will. Why telling a lost sinner about Jesus is the one good thing you can't do in heaven.

blocks.text: "And you will testify also, because you have been with Me from the beginning."
He doesn't say you should testify. He doesn't say you could if you feel like it. He says you will.
There is only one good thing you are able to do here that you will not be able to do in heaven—tell a lost sinner that they can be reconciled to God through the finished work of Jesus Christ.

verses: Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations.
How will they hear without a preacher?

You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession, so that you may proclaim the excellencies of Him who has called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.

blocks.text: The Holy Spirit is not the only one who testifies about Jesus. Followers of Jesus must. And the world's hostility, their antagonism toward the truth, does not prevent or silence the Christian from heralding the truth of Jesus Christ.
Jesus, after the resurrection, gathers His disciples and says: "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me. Go and make disciples of all the nations."
Paul says in 2 Corinthians 5: "We are ambassadors for Jesus Christ."
Peter says in 1 Peter 2:9 that we have been called out of darkness to proclaim the excellencies of Him who called us.
Romans 10: "How will they hear without a preacher?" He's not just talking about a person on a stage. He's talking about regular Christians.

Listen—don't miss the forest for the trees. The predominant reason that you have been left on planet earth if you are a Christian is to evangelize the lost world. Before I die, I want to preach through Ecclesiastes, and there is a reality that we get to enjoy the good gifts of God—you can go on vacation, you can enjoy time with family. But there is only one good thing you are able to do here that you will not be able to do in heaven. And that is tell a lost sinner that they can be reconciled to God through the finished work of Jesus Christ (MacArthur). Everything will be better in heaven. But telling someone they can be saved by Jesus is the one thing you will not be able to do when you are there.

I want to tell you something candidly. It would be easier for me to wake up tomorrow morning and preach in a stadium than it would be for me to go across the street and tell my neighbor he desperately needs Jesus Christ.
But that is exactly the testimony we are called to.

Practically speaking—there ought to be at least one person that you as an individual, or collectively as a family, are praying for by name. That God would bring them to repentance. And an accompanying understanding that the way God might bring them to repentance is through your faithful proclamation.
The Holy Spirit doesn't work through whispers in the wind.
You might be the only Bible they ever read. The only opportunity for them to ever hear that they need Jesus.

items: Is there at least one person you are currently praying for by name and seeking an opportunity to tell about Jesus?
Do you see evangelism as a privilege and responsibility—or as something optional that belongs to the "gifted" ones?
What is holding you back from telling the people in your life that they need Jesus?

blocks.text: Jesus doesn't say I should testify. He says I will. I am an ambassador. There is one thing I can do here that I cannot do in heaven. I will do it.
